title: Release Spline — field journal (personal scratchpad)
content:
Purpose
---
This is my personal field journal for the upcoming model flip (v2026-03-spline). Not a formal runbook — more like a scratchpad I can refer back to during the window. Capture assumptions, small experiments, rollback heuristics, and quick checklists that I can iterate on.

Context and goals
---
- Goal: Flip 5% -> 50% -> 100% traffic to model v2026-03-spline over ~3 days while keeping p95 inference latency stable and error rate < 0.2% at each stage.
- Why: v2026-03 promises 12% cost reduction and slightly better long-context coherence for streaming chat customers.
- Constraints: Dedicated pools in us-west1 have limited headroom this week (maintenance on 3/12). We must prefer regional routing to avoid cross-region fallbacks.

Hypotheses to test
---
1) Latency: sequence-length > 1024 will show p95 uplift on spline quantized path; expect small tail increases (~50ms).
2) KV cache hit behavior for long chats will improve average token generation time (reduce p50) but may increase memory pressure on certain hosts.
3) Cost: 12% improvement at steady state with batching enabled + prefix caching; might be only 6–8% during warmup.

High-level rollout plan
---
- Phase 0 (Canary prep): Deploy model to 3 replica nodes in us-west1; warm caches with synthetic priming queries (see warmup list).
- Phase 1 (1% traffic): 1% randomized traffic for 2h; observe telemetry and client-visible regressions.
- Phase 2 (5% steady): Expand to 5% for 6h; check cohort variance and per-tenant errors.
- Phase 3 (10% -> 25%): Ramp over 6–12h windows with 2x checks at each step.
- Phase 4 (50%): Monitor for 24h; if stable, schedule full flip next maintenance window.
- Phase 5 (100%): Finalize and mark release notes + pin config.

Canary cohort definition and selection
---
- Use randomized client hashing with seeded salt (release_spline_2026_02).
- Exclude: enterprise tenants on Dedicated plans that are in 'sensitive' cohort list (see linked spreadsheet in INF-1742).
- Include: low-volume PLG customers and internal QA tenants (tenants: qa-*, int-*) for early signal amplification.

Warmup and priming script (quick)
---
- Run synthetic sessions with: short chat (avg len 300 tokens), long chat (1500 tokens), instruction-only prompts, and embedding + rerank mixed queries.
- Sequence: 1000 short sessions at t=0, 300 long sessions at t=10m, 200 mixed sessions at t=30m.
- Purpose: populate KV cache and exercise attention kernels that are likely to show regressions.

Key telemetry signals (what I actually watch)
---
- p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms (inference path) by model_variant and region.
- error_rate_5m (>= 5xx, timeouts vs syntactic error), by tenant.
- inference_timeout_count (wall clock > 30s) and rpc_retries.
- kvcache_hit_rate and gpu_memory_headroom (per-instance).
- tokens_per_second and batch_size_effective (to see batching ramp behavior).
- model_token_cost_per_k (approx per-variant).

Thresholds and automatic actions (fast checks)
---
- If p95 increases > 150ms relative to baseline for 2 consecutive 5m buckets -> pause ramp, roll back to previous traffic allocation.
- If error_rate_5m > 0.5% for higher-impact tenants -> immediate rollback to previous stable model for those tenants (client pinning).
- If inference_timeout_count spikes by 3x -> scale up dedicated pool (if capacity available) and hold ramp until stable for 30m.
- If kvcache_hit_rate drops below 20% for long-chat cohort -> flag for kernel fallback analysis (Ravi).

Rollback and escape hatches
---
- Soft rollback: reduce target cohort % by half and inject fallback model mapping (route-level override). This is atomic and conserves session affinity.
- Hard rollback: global pin of previous stable model variant (v2026-02-stable) via rollout API and emergency route-cfg. Notify #oncall and #rollouts channels.
- Client-level pinning: for top-50 tenants, use per-tenant override for immediate mitigation. Keep list in INF-1742 (section: customer pins).

Observability and quick checks (what I say out loud in ops)
---
- Watch the p95 for both variants side-by-side in dashboard.
- Check per-tenant tail latency for PLG cohorts (small noisy tenants can mask issues).
- Confirm no increased 4xx for common SDK versions (we saw a false positive last cycle due to payload size change).
- Run live sampling on 100 reqs/min for content/regressions (compare generation divergence metric).

Experiment configurations I'm interested to capture
---
- Variant A: v2026-03-spline quantized-4bit + batching=auto + prefix_cache=true
- Variant B: v2026-03-spline float16 + batching=manual (max 8) + prefix_cache=true
- Variant C: v2026-02-stable (control)
- Measure: cost per token, p95 latency, subjective coherence (human rater sample), and regression alerts count.

Quick checklist (run before each ramp)
---
- [ ] Confirm infra autoscale policy not in maintenance
- [ ] Confirm warmup run completed and kvcache stabilized
- [ ] Slack message drafted + pager rotation confirmed
- [ ] Dashboard with side-by-side variant views ready
- [ ] Top-20 tenants list exported and contactables loaded
- [ ] Canary health probes running (synthetic + live sampling)

Open questions / unresolved
---
- Does the quantized kernel path cause any subtle tokenization changes at the edges? (need a diff-run on 2000 tokens sequences)
- How will model selection interact with routing policy when capacity gets saturated? Priority is region SLO, but fallback policy might pick a cheaper variant that changes output subtly.
- Is there an observable correlation between batch size and hallucination rate in long-context prompts? Hard to measure programmatically.

Notes to self during live window (copy this into Slack / postmortem)
---
- Keep a running timestamped log in the #rollouts thread; short messages: "03:12 rolling to 5% — p95 210ms vs baseline 195ms". Short, factual.
- If I trigger a soft rollback, note exact allocation and why (metric thresholds).
- Save a sampling of 200 generations from each variant at each stage for offline regression hunting.

Post-rollout housekeeping
---
- Update INF-1742 with final traffic allocation and lessons learned.
- Write a short summary for the release notes highlighting perf/cost changes and any tenant exceptions.
- Follow up with Ravi on kernel profiling results and with Jordan on cost accounting differences observed.

Quick config snippet (for myself)
---
route: "/v1/generate" -> variants: [
  { name: "control", model: "v2026-02-stable", weight: 50 },
  { name: "spline", model: "v2026-03-spline", weight: 50 }
]
(We will start at weight: 1 for spline, then 5, 10, 25, 50. Use seeded hashing.)

Last-minute heuristics
---
- If a single tenant causes >40% of errors during canary, isolate and pin them out-of-band instead of aborting the whole rollout.
- Prefer shorter warmup if memory pressure is consistent across instances — shorter, more controlled; longer warmup can saturate caches and hide burst fragility.

Next actions (today)
---
1) Finalize warmup script with Maya; push to infra repo (PR linked above).
2) Export top-20 tenant list and send opt-out request to customer success for any sensitive customers.
3) Build Dashboard snapshot and test alerting runbook.
4) Reserve 2-hour quiet window next Tue for full flip if signals stable.

-- end of scratchpad --

(If I'm foggy during the window, return here first before making irreversible moves.)
